name: _test_optional_filled_intlist
description: Representative ATen schema, verbatim: aten::_test_optional_filled_intlist(Tensor values, int[2]? addends) -> Tensor. This signature is representative and NOT exclusive. All registered ATen schemas, verbatim: aten::_test_optional_filled_intlist(Tensor values, int[2]? addends) -> Tensor ; aten::_test_optional_filled_intlist.out(Tensor values, int[2]? addends, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!). The original Gems pytest owns the full contract (overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation); do not narrow its coverage to this one signature. Semantics evidenced by the tests: `addends` is a host int operand that may be None, an int (the int[2]? fill) or an explicit int list. When `addends is None` the operator is a pure identity: it returns the input tensor object itself (`res_out is inp`) for any dtype, rank and shape, preserving shape, stride, storage offset, data pointer and dtype, and later in-place updates of the input are visible through the result. When `addends` is present, `values` must be a rank-1 int32 tensor and `values[i] + addends[i]` is computed per element, returning a fresh tensor with distinct storage; the addends operand must cover every element (the int[2]? fill only covers tensors of up to two elements, so an explicit list shorter than the tensor is rejected). Native dispatch is CPU only; CUDA and Meta raise NotImplementedError. The `.out` overload writes into the keyword-only `out` buffer (mutating it and returning that same buffer), resizes a non-view buffer to the result shape while respecting a view's shape/stride/storage offset, and copies rather than aliasing the input when `addends is None`. Errors remain defined by pytest: missing `addends` is rejected because optional describes the value, not omissibility; short addends, non-1-D values, non-int32 values, invalid addends types, non-tensor values and a wrong `out` dtype raise RuntimeError or TypeError as tested, while the missing autograd derivative raises RuntimeError as tested. The representative default overload declares no mutation and no declared alias; the identity aliasing under `addends=None` and the `.out` mutation are overload/argument-dependent and are therefore documented here rather than encoded as conditional effects.
